classificationReport.severityCriteria: C4 (High=asset theft/loss/compromise or direct attack path; Medium=protocol function/availability impacted or value leak with stated assumptions; Low/QA=state-handling, spec deviation, centralization)
classificationReport.lawHierarchyApplied: Law 1 (security) > Law 2 (story faithfulness) > Law 3 (owner trust / footguns)

downgradesFromProposed.reason: Deployment-script revert in a one-shot owner-operated migration. No assets stolen/lost/compromised: the script reverts atomically, broadcasts no bad state, owner sees the revert and stops. Impact is precisely 'protocol function/availability impacted' (migration cannot execute) — the C4 Medium definition. High is reserved for actual asset/exploit outcomes; a guaranteed fail-safe revert is the opposite of an asset-loss path. Time-criticality is an aggravator, not asset risk.

Same rationale as DEDUP-001: independent second fatal ABI-decode revert blocking the migration. Availability/function blocker, no funds at direct risk, fails loud and safe. Kept as a SEPARATE Medium (Law 1) — collapsing into DEDUP-001 would hide a distinct fatal blocker.

classificationReport.faithfulnessRouting: DEDUP-001, DEDUP-002, DEDUP-003 also tagged faithfulness:true (script/doc deviate from stated migration intent). They carry real availability/value impact so they keep their honest Medium severity (Law 1 over Law 2) AND are surfaced as F-XX spec-conformance entries — never buried in the QA/gas bundle.

classification.assetImpact: No direct asset loss. Old DOLA/USDC strategies and the V1 minter retain all principal and mint authority unchanged. Impact is to protocol FUNCTION/AVAILABILITY: the entire MigrateSaga2Deploy script aborts on a staticcall to a selector (0x88b57777 setAsideBufferRecipient) absent from the deployed strategy bytecode, so the 2.1 deployment cannot execute and the whole saga (2.2/2.3) is blocked.
attackPath: 1. Owner runs migrate:saga2.1-deploy against live mainnet.
2. _carryBuffer staticcalls setAsideBufferRecipient() (0x88b57777) on the deployed old DOLA/USDC strategy.
3. The getter is absent in deployed bytecode -> empty-data return -> ABI decode revert.
4. The transaction reverts atomically; no state is broadcast; the migration is dead-on-arrival.
classification.likelihood: high (deterministic) — reverts on every run against the live deployment; verified fork-confirmed.
classification.assumptions: Run against the actual deployed mainnet strategies (the in-scope target).
classification.externalRequirements: None beyond running the script as intended.
classification.aggravators: Migration is time-critical (2.2 must land in a totalWithdrawal window); a 2.1 DOA blocks the whole saga. Operational urgency, not asset risk.

classifiedFindings.justification: Fail-safe, loud, atomic revert: no funds stolen or lost, no half-migrated/split-brain state. This is the textbook C4 Medium — protocol function/availability impacted — not High. Downgraded from proposed High because nothing in C4's High definition (assets stolen/lost/compromised or a direct exploit path) is met; overstating to High would dilute the report (CRITICAL RULE 1). Also a faithfulness deviation: the script does not do what the migration intent states (carry buffer), so routed to F-XX while keeping Medium per Law 1.

classification.assetImpact: No direct asset loss. Impact is to protocol FUNCTION/AVAILABILITY: config replication (the script's stated purpose) cannot execute. The inline IMinterV1 interface decodes a 7-field stablecoinConfigs struct, but the deployed PhusdStableMinter V1 returns 4 fields -> ABI buffer-overrun revert in _registerOnV2. Second, independent fatal blocker.
attackPath: 1. Owner runs migrate:saga2.1-deploy against live mainnet (assume DEDUP-001 hypothetically resolved or reached independently).
2. _registerOnV2 calls stablecoinConfigs on the deployed V1 minter via the script's 7-field IMinterV1 declaration.
3. Deployed V1 returns a 4-field struct; the 7-field decode overruns the return buffer.
4. The call reverts atomically; config replication cannot proceed; migration aborts.
classification.likelihood: high (deterministic) — reverts on every run against the live deployment; verified fork-confirmed.
classification.assumptions: Run against the actual deployed mainnet V1 minter (the in-scope target).
classification.externalRequirements: None beyond running the script as intended.
classification.aggravators: Independent of DEDUP-001 — even if 001 were fixed, this separately bricks the migration. Same time-criticality aggravator.

classifiedFindings.justification: Same class as CLASS-001: a fail-safe atomic revert that impacts protocol function/availability, with no funds at direct risk. Medium, not High, under C4. Kept separate from DEDUP-001 per Law 1 — two independent fatal blockers; collapsing would hide one. Faithfulness deviation (script cannot replicate V1 config as intended) routed to F-XX; Medium retained per Law 1.

classification.assetImpact: Value/availability leak on the staker's liquidity cushion: the carried set-aside buffer is silently hardcoded to 10% while live on-chain old strategies use 25% — a 60% reduction of the below-par cushion. Only logged, never asserted/enforced. Not direct theft, but a degraded protective parameter that protects staker withdrawals.
attackPath: 1. Operator runs the migration believing they 'carry forward the existing buffer' (per inline comment / design doc S8, which wrongly states existing is 10%).
2. _carryBuffer applies the hardcoded 10% constant instead of reading the live 25%.
3. New strategies launch with a 60%-smaller set-aside buffer; the change is only logged, never asserted.
4. Under stress / below-par conditions, the reduced cushion increases withdrawal-shortfall risk for stakers.
classification.likelihood: medium — deterministic once the script can run (downstream of DEDUP-001/002 blockers), but the harmful consequence is silent and surprising to a competent non-malicious operator.
classification.assumptions: Operator trusts the 'carry forward' comment and the design doc; does not manually cross-check the live on-chain buffer.
classification.externalRequirements: Script must first be unblocked (DEDUP-001/002 resolved). Once running, the downgrade is automatic.
classification.footgunRationale: Non-obvious owner footgun (Law 3): the operator would be surprised that 'carry forward the existing buffer' silently halves-plus the live cushion. In scope as an operational hazard with safe-config guidance: read and assert the live setAsideBuffer rather than hardcoding 10%.

classifiedFindings.justification: Value leak with stated assumptions and an external requirement (script first unblocked) — C4 Medium. Classified by the impact it unlocks (degraded staker cushion), labeled a footgun with safe-config guidance, NOT a malicious-admin vector (Law 3). Faithfulness deviation (design doc/comment misstate live config) routed to F-XX; Medium retained per Law 1.

classification.assetImpact: No direct loss. Net-new ERC4626YieldStrategy instances and minterV2 are deployed without a pauser, leaving them unpausable. Reduced incident-response capability (no break-glass) on contracts that will hold all DOLA/USDC principal and the active phUSD mint authority.
attackPath: 1. Script deploys ysDolaV2/ysUsdcV2/minterV2 and never calls setPauser.
2. Contracts go live with pauser == address(0).
3. If a future incident requires pausing, no party can pause -> degraded response.
classification.likelihood: low — requires a separate future incident to bite; no standalone impact.
classification.assumptions: Verified NOT deferred-by-design (2.2/2.3 also never set the pauser).
classification.externalRequirements: A subsequent incident requiring the pause break-glass.
classification.footgunRationale: Missing runbook step on net-new critical contracts. In scope (Law 3) as an operational-availability footgun; prior batch-minter-migrate suppression (b31f507a) correctly does not carry — different entryPoint, net-new contracts, not deferred.

classifiedFindings.justification: Operational-availability / configuration footgun with no direct or standalone asset impact and a future-incident external requirement. Low/QA per C4. Retain in QA bundle with safe-config guidance (call setPauser post-deploy).

classification.assetImpact: No direct impact on its own. The script has no post-condition assertions on its most consequential writes (phUSD mint-authority swap, setMigrator, wiring) — fire-and-forget. A silent partial/incorrect write could go unnoticed at deploy time.
attackPath: 1. Script performs mint-authority swap + setMigrator + wiring.
2. No post-write assert verifies the resulting on-chain state matches intent.
3. A misconfiguration would only be caught later, not at deploy time.
classification.likelihood: low — state-handling/configuration-safety gap; amplifies other findings but causes nothing alone.
classification.externalRequirements: Requires a separate incorrect write to actually cause harm.

classifiedFindings.justification: Configuration-safety / state-handling gap (missing verification gate). No standalone impact. Low/QA per C4. Made more pointed by the two fork-confirmed ABI drifts on the same script, but the missing-assert issue itself is Low.

classification.assetImpact: No direct loss. The script is not idempotent and has no progress/checkpoint guard: a re-run redeploys everything, re-revokes/re-grants phUSD mint, and overwrites the handoff JSON. Produces a recoverable split-brain (second minterV2/strategies granted mint while addresses.ts + 2.2/2.3 reference the first).
attackPath: 1. Operator re-runs 2.1 (e.g. after a partial failure or ambiguity).
2. Script redeploys contracts, re-grants mint authority, overwrites the handoff JSON.
3. addresses.ts / 2.2 / 2.3 still reference the first deployment -> split-brain across the saga during the most fragile window.
classification.likelihood: low-to-medium — requires an operator re-run; departs from the project's own documented checkpoint/resilient-deployment pattern.
classification.assumptions: Operator re-runs the script without manual cleanup.
classification.externalRequirements: A re-run during the migration window.
classification.footgunRationale: Non-obvious operator footgun (Law 3): a re-run silently creating a split-brain is surprising. In scope as an operational hazard; safe-config guidance: add an idempotency/checkpoint guard before redeploying or re-granting mint.

classifiedFindings.justification: Operator footgun producing a recoverable split-brain, contingent on a re-run; no direct asset loss. Low/QA per C4. Retain in QA bundle with checkpoint-guard guidance. Lineage to the superseded route (YS-35 family) does not suppress — per-entryPoint fingerprint, saga-2.1 replaces that route.
